status.en: 74 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 35% more than the week before, most of them in Sanaa, Mokha and Marib.
status.nb: 74 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 35 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i Sanaa, Mokha og Marib.

summary.en: Houthis launched missile strikes on Riyadh airport, killing twelve people—including an airline captain—and wounding hundreds, prompting the airport’s closure and Saudi vows of a major response. The attacks were followed by Houthi threats to Saudi airspace and warnings that they could target other Saudi airports. Yemeni government forces reported advancing against the Houthis, while fighting spread to Yemen’s capital and other cities. The EU condemned the attack, describing it as part of Iran‑backed proxy aggression in the region. The conflict caused 918 battle‑related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Houthis lanserte missilangrep på Riyadh flyplass, og drepte tolv personer—inkludert en flykaptein—og såret hundrevis, noe som førte til at flyplassen ble stengt og Saudi-Arabia lovet et stort svar. Angrepene ble fulgt av trusler fra Houthi‑ene mot saudisk luftrom og advarsler om at de kunne ramme andre saudiske flyplasser. Jemens regjeringsstyrker rapporterte fremrykkinger mot Houthi‑ene, mens kampene spredte seg til Jemens hovedstad og andre byer. EU fordømte angrepet og beskrev det som en del av Irans støttede proxy‑aggressjon i regionen. Konflikten forårsaket 918 dødsfall i kamprelaterte handlinger i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Yemeni civil war (2014–present)
background.extract: The Yemeni civil war is an ongoing multilateral civil war that began in late 2014 mainly between the Rashad al-Alimi-led Presidential Leadership Council and the Mahdi al-Mashat-led Supreme Political Council, along with their respective supporters and allies. Both sides claim to constitute the official government of Yemen while the Presidential Leadership Council is recognized by the United Nations as the official government.
